summary: 1. Replace academic discovery premises ('Scientists found...') with immediate, concrete paradoxes or counter-intuitive assertions ('A car that folds keeps you safer', 'T. rex couldn't run'). 2. Kill all preamble and subordinate clauses: keep hook sentence 1 under 14 words and deliver the core conflict before second 2. 3. Target visceral, high-affinity topics that pit physical intuition against reality (cars, crashes, T. rex, immediate bodily sensations) rather than passive observational science (astronomy, ponds, infrastructure). 4. Format titles around high-contrast mechanical questions or counter-intuitive rules ('Why Double Speed Means 4x Braking Distance') rather than sensational discovery hype with emojis. 5. Keep target video length strictly between 15–25 seconds; all videos with stayed_pct > 50% peaked within this duration band, while 30+ second scripts suffered swiping drop-off.
winning_hooks: The real T. rex probably couldn't run. Not even a jog. (Immediate myth-busting with an emphatic, short cadence)
A car that folds up in a crash keeps you safer than one that doesn't. (Instant paradox challenging visual intuition)
Your eyes are leaking right now, and your brain is hiding it. (Direct 'you' framing tied to an active bodily sensation)
Drive twice as fast, and your car needs four times as far to stop. (High-contrast, concrete numerical rule delivered in 13 words)
avoid: Slow narrative preambles and multi-clause setups (e.g., 'Pluto seemed like our solar system's edge, yet astronomers are investigating...')
Vague, low-stakes claims that state the obvious (e.g., 'Most James Webb images hold secrets')
Abstract science history or passive research framing ('Scientists just found...', 'Did Scientists Find Real Dinosaur Blood?')
Niche industrial/infrastructure explainers that lack immediate human stakes (e.g., 'Why Highway Guardrails Have Heavy End Boxes')
next_experiment: Test Hook Syntax on the same topic: Take a physics/car topic and A/B test Hook A (Myth-Busting Assertion: 'Braking hard in the rain doesn't stop you faster—it locks your tires.') vs. Hook B (Hypothetical Narrative: 'Imagine you are driving 60 mph on wet asphalt when a deer jumps out.') while holding the script under 20 seconds and tracking stayed_pct differences.
